record.title: NP-F550-form-factor 2S Li-ion pack, 7.2 V nominal, 2600 mAh — the Microduck's removable battery (Sony InfoLITHIUM L-series shape; maker of the fitted pack unidentified)
record.why: THE FORM FACTOR IS KNOWN, THE FITTED PACK IS NOT. Pollen's press kit says the battery is a removable NP-F550, 2600 mAh, ~1 h (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §9; docs/PARTS.md row 35), and the runtime maps 6.6–8.2 V under load to 0–100 % (model.rs:99-128) — a 2-series Li-ion pack. But 'NP-F550' names Sony's ORIGINAL L-series pack, which Sony rates 1500 mAh / 10.8 Wh, so a 2600 mAh 'NP-F550' is necessarily a THIRD-PARTY pack in Sony's shape, and no source names whose. This folder therefore carries: (1) a representative vendor page for a 2600 mAh 7.2 V pack in this shape — Duracell DR5 'Replacement Sony NP-F330/NP-F550 Battery 7.2V 2600mAh', FETCHED 2026-09-02 (docs/, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json), quoted verbatim in electrical.part.json; (2) a second vendor sheet, Deity's NP-F550 (3350 mAh, LG 18650 cells), as evidence of what cell type these packs use — NOT the fitted pack; (3) Sony's own specification page as CANNOT DETERMINE: every Sony host tried (sony.com.au, sony.co.uk, sony.com, sony-asia.com, sony.com.hk, sony.jp, pro.sony, electronics.sony.com) answered 403 or 404 to curl and to WebFetch on 2026-09-02 — the URLs are in electrical.part.json unknowns, and a search-engine snippet is not a source. WHAT SETTLES IT: the label on a shipped pack (maker, cell, Wh, certification marks), or Pollen naming the supplier. GEOMETRY CLOSED 2026-09-02: the mesh measures 38.6085 x 20.5681 x 70.8050 mm and the bay around it 38.7310 x 21.1721 x 70.9231 mm (tools/measure_battery_bay.py, evidence/battery-bay.json). A published NP-F550 body fits with 0.1231 mm to spare; a published NP-F970 body interferes by 19.829 mm in its best orientation. See record.finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed. What remains open is only WHICH F550-shape pack.
record.subsector_why: the shelf already uses battery_pack for lipo_2s_shorty_pack.
record.lifecycle_why: the fitted pack's maker is unknown, so its lifecycle cannot be checked. Duracell's DR5 page carried no lifecycle statement on 2026-09-02.
record.origin_why: the electrical figures in electrical.part.json come from FETCHED vendor pages (Duracell DR5 page, Deity NP-F550 sheet), byte for byte in docs/ with sha256 in PROVENANCE.json. The dimensions come from Pollen's own simulation mesh (a vendor artefact, CC BY-SA-NC, cited in docs/PARTS.md). Not 'standard': no published standard defines the NP-F shape. Not 'measured': no physical pack has been on a bench here.
record.bbox_basis: MEASURED 2026-09-02 (lane C), not cited: Pollen's np_f970.stl read directly (reference/pollen-microduck-simulator/meshes/np_f970.stl, binary STL, 4953 triangles, metres x1000) and its axis-aligned box taken in its own file frame. 38.6085 x 20.5681 x 70.8050 mm. Order is [width, thickness, length]. Supersedes the earlier one-decimal figure copied through docs/PARTS.md row 35. Duracell's DR5 page states '70 x 38 x 20 mm' and nextbatteries.com's NP-F550 spec table '70.80 x 38.50 x 21.00mm' (fetched 2026-09-02) — the mesh sits inside the latter on every axis.
record.used_by_why: placed in the trunk on power_support (docs/PARTS.md rows 3, 35).

finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.verdict: CLOSED — the fitted pack is an NP-F550-class L-series slim body, and Pollen's mesh filename np_f970 is wrong
finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.why_it_was_open: COMPARISON.html §5 finding 2: the simulator's battery mesh is called np_f970 while every Pollen word about the product says NP-F550. Two different Sony packs.
finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.the_measurement: MEASURED 2026-09-02 by tools/measure_battery_bay.py off Pollen's own meshes placed by Pollen's own MJCF transforms (spec/mesh-placements.json, body trunk_base), result evidence/battery-bay.json: the pack mesh is 38.6085 (X) x 20.5681 (Y) x 70.8050 (Z) mm in its own frame, and the bay around it is 38.7310 x 21.1721 x 70.9231 mm — bounded on X by power_support both sides (0.0492 / 0.0733 mm), on Y by power_support (0.4948) and left_shell (0.1092), on Z by banana_pcb_locker (0.0145) and power_support (0.1036). Nothing is open.

the_two_candidate_bodies.NP-F550: 70.80 x 38.50 x 21.00 mm — nextbatteries.com/products/sony-np-f550-battery spec table, 7.4 V, 2000 mAh, Li-ion, $17.90, fetched 2026-09-02. FITS the measured bay with 0.1231 mm to spare on the tightest axis.
the_two_candidate_bodies.NP-F970: 70.85 x 38.40 x 58.56 mm — nextbatteries.com/products/sony-np-f970-battery spec table, 7.4 V, 6600 mAh, Li-ion, fetched 2026-09-02. DOES NOT FIT in any orientation: 19.829 mm of interference at best. The two packs share 70.8 x 38.4; only the third dimension differs, and it is the one the trunk constrains to 21.1721 mm.

finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.so: The geometry, not an opinion, settles it. A 25 cm robot whose trunk gives the pack 21.17 mm of depth cannot take a 58.56 mm F970. The filename is legacy; the body is F550.
finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.still_cannot_determine: WHICH F550-shape pack (maker, cell, mAh, protection circuit, certification marks) — unchanged, see record.why. A shipped pack's label settles it.
finding_2_the_mesh_is_misnamed.consequence_for_the_bom: The bought line is 'NP-F550-form-factor 2S Li-ion pack, 7.2/7.4 V nominal'. It is a commodity with many suppliers; the design constraint is the 70.9231 x 38.7310 x 21.1721 mm bay, which several catalogue packs exceed — nextbatteries' own 3350 mAh F550-shape listings and Jupio's ProLine 3350 mAh are the ones to check, because extra capacity in this shell usually comes as extra thickness and the bay has 0.1231 mm.
